rows: Return the JSON value of the node at a JSONPath-ish `path` (e.g. '$.0.2') within a blob, or JSON null if the path does not resolve.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the decoded JSON value of the node located at `path` within a BER/CER/DER blob. `path` is the JSONPath-ish locator produced by `tlv()` (e.g. `$` for the root, `$.0.2` for the third child of the first child). Returns JSON `null` when the path does not resolve or the blob is malformed.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Get the value at a node path, e.g. `at_path(payload, '$.0.2')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Pull the node at path '$.0' (the first child — the INTEGER) of a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }`.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.at_path(from_hex('3003020105'), '$.0') AS node;"}]
rows.vgi.title: ASN.1 Value at Path

rows: Return the embedded DER certificates of a CMS SignedData as a LIST(BLOB) — the join key to vgi-x509 (hash each with sha256).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the list of embedded DER certificates carried in a CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData (RFC 5652) as a `LIST(BLOB)`. Each element is a complete X.509 certificate you can hash (sha256) and join to a vgi-x509 fingerprint, or re-feed to asn1.decode. Empty list for a non-SignedData blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Get the embedded CMS certificates as a `LIST(BLOB)`, e.g. `cms_certs(data)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Extract the embedded certificate LIST<BLOB> from a CMS blob (an empty list for this minimal id-data ContentInfo, which carries no certs).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.cms_certs(from_hex('301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869')) AS certs;"}]
rows.vgi.title: CMS Embedded Certificates

rows: Return the encapsulated eContent (BLOB) of a CMS SignedData — often a nested CMS/DER, re-feed to decode(). NULL when absent.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the encapsulated content (`eContent`) bytes of a CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData (RFC 5652) as a `BLOB`. This is the signed payload — often itself a nested CMS or DER structure you can re-feed to asn1.decode. NULL when no eContent is present (detached signature) or the blob is not a SignedData.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Get the CMS signed payload bytes, e.g. `cms_content(data)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Extract the encapsulated eContent BLOB from a CMS SignedData (NULL for this minimal id-data ContentInfo, which wraps no SignedData).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.cms_content(from_hex('301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869')) AS econtent;"}]
rows.vgi.title: CMS Encapsulated Content

rows: Decode a CMS / PKCS#7 ContentInfo to JSON (named content_type + dispatched content).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a CMS / PKCS#7 ContentInfo (RFC 5652) into a JSON projection: the named content_type (signedData, envelopedData, TSTInfo, …) and the dispatched content tree. Use cms_signers() / cms_certs() / cms_content() to shred a SignedData. Signatures are surfaced, never verified.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode a CMS/PKCS#7 blob to JSON, e.g. `cms_decode(data)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode a minimal CMS ContentInfo (content_type 'id-data') into JSON.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.cms_decode(from_hex('301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869')) AS info;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode CMS / PKCS#7

rows: Shred a CMS SignedData into one row per SignerInfo

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Shred a CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData (RFC 5652) into one row per SignerInfo: the signer's identity (IssuerAndSerial or SubjectKeyIdentifier), the named digest/signature algorithm OIDs, the well-known signed attributes (contentType, messageDigest, signingTime) and the rest as JSON, the signature bytes, and signer_cert_sha256 — the SHA-256 of the matching embedded certificate, a direct join key to a vgi-x509 fingerprint. The signature is surfaced, never verified. The blob argument is a literal/scalar; for bulk per-row use the scalar cms_decode().
rows.vgi.doc_md: Shred CMS SignerInfos into rows (the vgi-x509 join surface). Key columns: `digest_alg`, `sig_alg`, `signing_time`, `signer_cert_sha256`, `signature`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Shred a CMS SignedData into one row per SignerInfo and project the signer identity kind and the named digest/signature algorithms.","sql":"SELECT signer_sid, digest_alg, sig_alg FROM asn1.main.cms_signers(from_hex('304d0201013100301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869a0053003020105312c302a020101800401020304300b0609608648016503040201300d06092a864886f70d01010105000403aabbcc')) ORDER BY signer_sid;"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"description":"SignerInfo version (CMSVersion).","name":"version","type":"INTEGER"},{"description":"Signer identifier kind.","name":"signer_sid","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Signer cert issuer (CN=…,O=…).","name":"signer_issuer","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Signer cert serial (decimal).","name":"signer_serial","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Subject key identifier (hex), if SKID-based.","name":"signer_skid","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Named digest algorithm OID.","name":"digest_alg","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Named signature algorithm OID.","name":"sig_alg","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"signingTime signed attribute (UTC).","name":"signing_time","type":"TIMESTAMP"},{"description":"contentType (eContentType / signed attr).","name":"content_type","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"messageDigest signed attribute bytes.","name":"message_digest","type":"BLOB"},{"description":"The signature bytes (surfaced, not verified).","name":"signature","type":"BLOB"},{"description":"SHA-256 (hex) of the matching embedded cert — join to vgi-x509.","name":"signer_cert_sha256","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Remaining signed attributes as JSON.","name":"signed_attrs","type":"VARCHAR"}]
rows.vgi.title: CMS Signers

rows: Decode a BER/CER/DER blob to its nested typed JSON projection (the 'auto' mode). NULL → NULL; a malformed blob yields {error,kind}. Call the two-argument overload to choose a different mode.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode any BER / CER / DER blob into JSON. The optional second argument `mode` is one of 'auto' (default), 'struct', 'json' — all returning the clean nested typed projection (SEQUENCE→array, primitives→their scalar value, OID→dotted string, time→ISO-8601, OCTET/BIT STRING→base64url) — or 'tlv', which returns the flat list of TLV nodes (path, class, tag, length, value). A stable JSON column type, so it never aborts a scan: NULL input yields NULL and a malformed blob yields a JSON object {error, kind} rather than an error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode an ASN.1 blob to JSON, e.g. `decode(payload)` or `decode(payload,'tlv')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` to a nested JSON tree (yields the JSON array `[5]`).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.decode(from_hex('3003020105')) AS decoded;"},{"description":"Decode a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` with mode 'tlv' to its flat list of TLV nodes (path, class, tag, length, value).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.decode(from_hex('3003020105'), 'tlv') AS nodes;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode ASN.1

rows: Decode a BER/CER/DER blob to JSON with an explicit output `mode` ∈ {auto, struct, json, tlv}: auto/struct/json return the nested typed JSON projection; tlv returns the flat TLV-node list. NULL → NULL; a malformed blob yields {error,kind}.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode any BER / CER / DER blob into JSON. The optional second argument `mode` is one of 'auto' (default), 'struct', 'json' — all returning the clean nested typed projection (SEQUENCE→array, primitives→their scalar value, OID→dotted string, time→ISO-8601, OCTET/BIT STRING→base64url) — or 'tlv', which returns the flat list of TLV nodes (path, class, tag, length, value). A stable JSON column type, so it never aborts a scan: NULL input yields NULL and a malformed blob yields a JSON object {error, kind} rather than an error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode an ASN.1 blob to JSON, e.g. `decode(payload)` or `decode(payload,'tlv')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` to a nested JSON tree (yields the JSON array `[5]`).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.decode(from_hex('3003020105')) AS decoded;"},{"description":"Decode a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` with mode 'tlv' to its flat list of TLV nodes (path, class, tag, length, value).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.decode(from_hex('3003020105'), 'tlv') AS nodes;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode ASN.1

rows: Render an indented human-debug TLV dump of a blob in the default openssl `asn1parse` style (offset, depth, header/length, tag name, primitive value). A malformed blob renders a parse-error line, never an error. Pass a second argument to choose the 'dumpasn1' style.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Render a BER/CER/DER blob as an indented human-debug TLV dump — the primary triage surface, preserving tags, lengths, raw bytes, and indefinite-length markers. The optional second argument `format` is 'openssl' (default; mirrors `openssl asn1parse`: offset, depth, header/length, tag name, primitive value) or 'dumpasn1' (Gutmann's annotated indentation, with OID names from the bundled registry). A malformed blob renders a short parse-error line instead of erroring.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Produce an indented TLV dump of a blob, e.g. `dump(payload)` or `dump(payload,'dumpasn1')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Produce an openssl-asn1parse-style dump of a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }`.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105')) AS text;"},{"description":"Dump a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` in dumpasn1 (Gutmann annotated) style.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105'), 'dumpasn1') AS text;"}]
rows.vgi.title: ASN.1 Dump

rows: Render an indented human-debug TLV dump of a blob in an explicit `format` ∈ {openssl, dumpasn1}: openssl mirrors `openssl asn1parse`; dumpasn1 mirrors Gutmann's annotated style with OID names. A malformed blob renders a parse-error line, never an error.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Render a BER/CER/DER blob as an indented human-debug TLV dump — the primary triage surface, preserving tags, lengths, raw bytes, and indefinite-length markers. The optional second argument `format` is 'openssl' (default; mirrors `openssl asn1parse`: offset, depth, header/length, tag name, primitive value) or 'dumpasn1' (Gutmann's annotated indentation, with OID names from the bundled registry). A malformed blob renders a short parse-error line instead of erroring.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Produce an indented TLV dump of a blob, e.g. `dump(payload)` or `dump(payload,'dumpasn1')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Produce an openssl-asn1parse-style dump of a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }`.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105')) AS text;"},{"description":"Dump a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` in dumpasn1 (Gutmann annotated) style.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105'), 'dumpasn1') AS text;"}]

rows: Whether a blob is well-formed under the default DER encoding rules (canonical: minimal lengths, no indefinite length). NULL → NULL; a malformed blob returns FALSE, never an error. Pass a second argument to validate as 'ber' or 'cer' instead.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return whether a blob is well-formed under the named encoding rules. The optional second argument `rules` is 'der' (default), 'cer', or 'ber'; 'der'/'cer' additionally enforce canonical constraints (minimal length encoding, no indefinite length). Cheap and total — a malformed blob returns FALSE, never an error; NULL input returns NULL.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Check a blob's well-formedness under encoding rules, e.g. `is_valid(data,'der')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Check that a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` is well-formed (returns true).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(from_hex('3003020105')) AS valid;"},{"description":"Check that a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` is valid under the strict DER rules (returns true).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(from_hex('3003020105'), 'der') AS valid;"}]
rows.vgi.title: ASN.1 Valid?

rows: Whether a blob is well-formed under an explicit `rules` ∈ {ber, cer, der}; der/cer also enforce canonical constraints (minimal lengths, no indefinite length). NULL → NULL; a malformed blob returns FALSE, never an error.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return whether a blob is well-formed under the named encoding rules. The optional second argument `rules` is 'der' (default), 'cer', or 'ber'; 'der'/'cer' additionally enforce canonical constraints (minimal length encoding, no indefinite length). Cheap and total — a malformed blob returns FALSE, never an error; NULL input returns NULL.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Check a blob's well-formedness under encoding rules, e.g. `is_valid(data,'der')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Check that a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` is well-formed (returns true).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(from_hex('3003020105')) AS valid;"},{"description":"Check that a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` is valid under the strict DER rules (returns true).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(from_hex('3003020105'), 'der') AS valid;"}]
rows.vgi.title: ASN.1 Valid?

rows: Decode a Kerberos V5 message to JSON, dispatched on its [APPLICATION n] message tag.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a Kerberos V5 message (RFC 4120) by dispatching on its [APPLICATION n] tag (Ticket, AS-REQ/REP, TGS-REQ/REP, AP-REQ/REP, KRB-ERROR, …) into a JSON projection. Encrypted parts are left as opaque bytes — nothing is decrypted.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode a Kerberos message to JSON, e.g. `krb_decode(blob)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode an [APPLICATION 1] Kerberos Ticket (tkt-vno 5) into JSON (msg_type 'Ticket').","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.krb_decode(from_hex('61073005a003020105')) AS msg;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode Kerberos Message

rows: Parse the outer Kerberos Ticket (RFC 4120) into a STRUCT(tkt_vno, realm, sname, name_type, enc_part_etype, enc_part_kvno, enc_part_cipher). The EncTicketPart stays encrypted (etype named, cipher as BLOB).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Parse the outer Kerberos `Ticket` ([APPLICATION 1], RFC 4120) into a typed `STRUCT`: ticket version, realm, service principal name + name-type, and the EncryptedData envelope (named etype, kvno, and the still-encrypted cipher as a `BLOB` — nothing is decrypted). NULL for a non-Ticket blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Project the outer Kerberos Ticket into a `STRUCT`, e.g. `krb_ticket(blob)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Project the outer [APPLICATION 1] Ticket envelope to a STRUCT (here tkt_vno = 5; realm/sname/enc-part NULL on this minimal ticket).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.krb_ticket(from_hex('61073005a003020105')) AS ticket;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Kerberos Ticket

rows: STRUCT(tkt_vno BIGINT, realm VARCHAR, sname VARCHAR, name_type VARCHAR, enc_part_etype VARCHAR, enc_part_kvno BIGINT, enc_part_cipher BLOB)
Decode the first LDAPMessage of a blob to JSON (message_id, protocolOp, dn/filter/…).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode the first LDAPMessage of a blob (RFC 4511) into a JSON projection: message_id, the protocolOp name, plus dn / scope / RFC 4515 filter / attributes / result fields as applicable. Use ldap_messages() to fan a multi-message segment into rows.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode an LDAP message to JSON, e.g. `ldap_decode(blob)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode a real LDAP searchRequest into JSON (RFC 4515 filter '(uid=jdoe)').","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.ldap_decode(from_hex('3033020102632e040a64633d6578616d706c650a01020a0100020100020100010100a30b040375696404046a646f6530040402636e')) AS msg;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode LDAP Message

rows: Fan a blob's LDAP messages into one row each

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Fan a blob (one segment may carry several LDAPMessages, RFC 4511) into one row per message: message_id, the protocolOp op name, plus dn / scope / RFC 4515 filter / attributes / result fields as applicable. The blob argument is a literal/scalar; for bulk per-row shredding of a column use the scalar ldap_decode().
rows.vgi.doc_md: Shred LDAP messages into rows. Columns: `message_id`, `op`, `dn`, `scope`, `filter`, `attributes`, `result_code`, `matched_dn`, `diagnostic`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Shred an LDAP SearchRequest into rows and project the operation, base DN, and RFC 4515 filter.","sql":"SELECT op, dn, filter FROM asn1.main.ldap_messages(from_hex('3033020102632e040a64633d6578616d706c650a01020a0100020100020100010100a30b040375696404046a646f6530040402636e')) ORDER BY message_id;"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"description":"The LDAP messageID.","name":"message_id","type":"INTEGER"},{"description":"The protocolOp name, e.g. SearchRequest.","name":"op","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"The base/object DN (op-dependent).","name":"dn","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Search scope (SearchRequest).","name":"scope","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"RFC 4515 filter string (SearchRequest).","name":"filter","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Requested/returned attribute names.","name":"attributes","type":"VARCHAR[]"},{"description":"Named LDAPResult code (result ops).","name":"result_code","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"The matchedDN (result ops).","name":"matched_dn","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"The diagnosticMessage (result ops).","name":"diagnostic","type":"VARCHAR"}]

rows: SELECT op, dn, filter FROM asn1.main.ldap_messages(from_hex('3033020102632e040a64633d6578616d706c650a01020a0100020100020100010100a30b040375696404046a646f6530040402636e')) ORDER BY message_id;
Decode an OCSP request or response to JSON (status, responder, per-cert responses).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode an OCSP request or response (RFC 6960) into a JSON projection: response_status, producedAt, responder_id, and a responses list (per-cert serial, issuer hashes, cert_status good/revoked/unknown, revocation time/reason, this/next update). Signature surfaced, not verified.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode an OCSP message to JSON, e.g. `ocsp_decode(blob)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode a minimal OCSPResponse into JSON (response_status 'successful').","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.ocsp_decode(from_hex('30030a0100')) AS msg;"}]

rows: Resolve a friendly OID name to its dotted form from the bundled registry, or NULL if unknown.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Resolve a friendly OID name (e.g. 'sha256WithRSAEncryption', case-insensitive) to its dotted OBJECT IDENTIFIER (e.g. '1.2.840.113549.1.1.11') from the bundled registry. Returns NULL for a name not in the registry. The inverse of oid_name().
rows.vgi.doc_md: Resolve a name to a dotted OID, e.g. `oid('id-at-commonName')` → '2.5.4.3'.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Resolve a name to '2.5.4.3'.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.oid('id-at-commonName');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Name → OID

rows: Resolve a dotted OID to its friendly name from the bundled registry, or NULL if unknown.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Resolve a dotted OBJECT IDENTIFIER (e.g. '1.2.840.113549.1.1.11') to its friendly name (e.g. 'sha256WithRSAEncryption') from the bundled registry of signature/digest algorithms, X.500 attribute types, content types, EKUs, curves, and SNMP/MIB anchors. Returns NULL for an OID not in the registry. The inverse of oid().
rows.vgi.doc_md: Resolve a dotted OID to a name, e.g. `oid_name('2.5.4.3')` → 'id-at-commonName'.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Resolve an OID to 'sha256WithRSAEncryption'.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.oid_name('1.2.840.113549.1.1.11');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Resolve OID to Friendly Name

rows: Return every OBJECT IDENTIFIER in a blob as a LIST of STRUCT(oid, name, path) — the OID inventory / join surface.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return every OBJECT IDENTIFIER in a BER/CER/DER blob as a `LIST` of `STRUCT(oid, name, path)`: the dotted OID, its friendly name resolved from the bundled registry (NULL if unknown), and its node path. The inventory / join surface — e.g. find every blob using a deprecated `sha1WithRSAEncryption` signature. Empty list for a malformed blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Inventory the OIDs in a blob, e.g. `oids(data)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Inventory every OID in an AlgorithmIdentifier blob — here 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 (sha256WithRSAEncryption), with its resolved name and node path.","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.oids(from_hex('300d06092a864886f70d01010b0500')) AS oids;"}]
rows.vgi.title: ASN.1 OID Inventory

rows: Split a PEM bundle into its DER blocks (idx, label, der)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Split a PEM bundle (text) into its `-----BEGIN <label>-----` blocks, base64-decoding each body to DER — one row per block: idx, label, der. The bridge from text armor to the DER scalars (decode/cms_decode/…). Blocks with an unparseable body are skipped.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Split a PEM bundle into DER blocks. Columns: `idx`, `label`, `der`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Split a one-block PEM bundle and list each block's index, label, and decoded DER length.","sql":"SELECT idx, label, octet_length(der) AS der_bytes FROM asn1.main.pem_decode('-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' || chr(10) || 'AQID' || chr(10) || '-----END CERTIFICATE-----') ORDER BY idx;"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"description":"Zero-based index of the PEM block within the bundle.","name":"idx","type":"INTEGER"},{"description":"The block label, e.g. 'CERTIFICATE' or 'PRIVATE KEY'.","name":"label","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"The base64-decoded DER bytes of the block (feed to asn1.decode).","name":"der","type":"BLOB"}]
rows.vgi.title: Decode PEM Bundle

rows: SELECT idx, label, octet_length(der) AS der_bytes FROM asn1.main.pem_decode('-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' || chr(10) || 'AQID' || chr(10) || '-----END CERTIFICATE-----') ORDER BY idx;
Return the label of the first PEM block in a text (e.g. 'CERTIFICATE'), or NULL if there is no PEM block.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the label of the first `-----BEGIN <label>-----` block in a PEM text (e.g. 'CERTIFICATE', 'PRIVATE KEY'), or NULL when the text contains no PEM block. Use pem_decode() to split a bundle into its DER blocks.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Get the first PEM block's label, e.g. `pem_label(armor)` → 'CERTIFICATE'.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Identify the label of the first PEM block in a text (returns 'CERTIFICATE').","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.pem_label('-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' || chr(10) || 'MIIBAg==' || chr(10) || '-----END CERTIFICATE-----') AS label;"}]

Walk a PKCS#12 keystore into one row per SafeBag

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Walk a PKCS#12 keystore (PFX → AuthenticatedSafe → SafeContents → SafeBag) into one row per bag: bag_type (keyBag, pkcs8ShroudedKeyBag, certBag, crlBag, …), the friendlyName / localKeyID attributes, the named key algorithm, and — for cert bags — cert_sha256 (a join key to vgi-x509). Structural only: NEVER surfaces plaintext key material and decrypts nothing. The blob argument is a literal/scalar.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Walk a PKCS#12 keystore's bags (no key material). Columns: `bag_type`, `friendly_name`, `local_key_id`, `alg`, `cert_sha256`, `encrypted`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Walk a minimal PKCS#12 PFX and list each SafeBag's type, encryption flag, and (for cert bags) the vgi-x509 join hash.","sql":"SELECT bag_type, encrypted, cert_sha256 FROM asn1.main.pkcs12_bags(from_hex('3051020103304c06092a864886f70d010701a03f043d303b303906092a864886f70d010701a02c042a30283026060b2a864886f70d010c0a0103a0173015060a2a864886f70d01091601a00704053003020105')) ORDER BY bag_type;"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"description":"SafeBag type, e.g. certBag, pkcs8ShroudedKeyBag.","name":"bag_type","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"friendlyName attribute, if present.","name":"friendly_name","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"localKeyID attribute (hex), if present.","name":"local_key_id","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Named key algorithm (key bags).","name":"alg","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"SHA-256 (hex) of the cert (cert bags) — join to vgi-x509.","name":"cert_sha256","type":"VARCHAR"},{"description":"Whether the bag's key material is encrypted.","name":"encrypted","type":"BOOLEAN"}]
rows.vgi.title: PKCS#12 Bags

rows: Structural PKCS#8 info: STRUCT(version, algorithm, params JSON, public_key BLOB, encrypted BOOL, kdf, enc_alg). Plaintext private-key octets are NEVER surfaced; encrypted keys name their PBES2/PBKDF2 OIDs.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo (RFC 5208) or EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo into a typed `STRUCT`: version, the named key algorithm, its params as JSON, an optional surfaced public key (never the private key), an `encrypted` flag, and — for encrypted keys — the named PBES2 `kdf` and `enc_alg` OIDs. No decryption; plaintext key material is never exposed.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Inspect PKCS#8 key structure (no key material), e.g. `pkcs8_info(blob)`.

rows: Structured well-formedness of a blob: STRUCT(ok BOOL, error VARCHAR, kind VARCHAR). kind ∈ {truncated, trailing-bytes, invalid-tag, length-overflow, indefinite-in-der, non-canonical, bad-time, bad-oid, bad-utf8, nesting-limit, alloc-limit}. Never errors.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the structured well-formedness of a blob: `STRUCT(ok, error, kind)`. On failure `ok` is false and `kind` classifies the problem — truncated, trailing-bytes, invalid-tag, length-overflow, indefinite-in-der, non-canonical, bad-time, bad-oid, bad-utf8, nesting-limit, or alloc-limit — with a human `error` message. Total: a malformed (even hostile) blob returns ok=false, never crashing the scan; NULL input yields a NULL struct.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Triage a blob's well-formedness with a failure kind, e.g. `well_formed(data)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Triage a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }`: returns STRUCT(ok=true, error=NULL, kind=NULL).","sql":"SELECT asn1.main.well_formed(from_hex('3003020105')) AS w;"}]
